narrative: Inventory optimization analysis for material PL1__MD24E079 reveals an intermittent-moderate demand pattern with mean daily demand of 1327.95 units (CV=0.223). Lead time exhibits unstable variability (CV=0.633, mean=1.53 days), requiring a conservative safety stock of 2207 units to maintain a 95% service level. The optimized policy recommends increasing order quantity from 7497 (MOQ-constrained SAP) to 15443 units (storage-capacity constrained), which reduces order frequency from 44.3 to 21.5 orders per year. This delivers annual cost savings of $521.16 (17.8%), despite higher holding costs, through reduced ordering frequency. Safety lead time analysis suggests reducing SAP's 4-day buffer to 1.66 days, as current empirical data shows lower lead time variability than assumed in the legacy system.
warnings: Order quantity constrained by storage capacity (reduced from 15752 to 15443)

research_insights.selected_model: Classical EOQ with combined LT-Demand variability
research_insights.selection_rationale: Approximately normal demand distribution (CV=0.22) with unstable lead times justifies safety stock formula incorporating both sources of variance.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity constraint binds at full utilization (17,650 units). Any safety stock increase requires order quantity reduction.
